{{Recipe}}

'''Mutura''' is a traditional Kenyan sausage and a type of blood sausage made by stuffing cleaned animal intestines with minced [[Cookbook:Meat|meat]], [[Cookbook:Spice|spices]], and sometimes fresh animal blood, then grilling it over charcoal. It is one of the most popular street foods in Kenya, especially in Nairobi and central Kenya.

==Ingredients==
* 500 g beef, goat meat, or mixed meat, finely chopped
* 200 g tripe or organ meat, finely chopped
* 1 cup fresh animal blood (optional)
* 1 large onion, finely chopped
* 2 cloves [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], minced
* 1 teaspoon grated ginger
* 1–2 green chilies or chili powder
* 1 teaspoon black pepper
* Salt to taste
* 2 tablespoons chopped coriander leaves (optional)

==Equipment==
* Knife
* Cutting board
* Mixing bowl
* Cooking pot
* Charcoal grill or barbecue
* Skewers or kitchen twine

==Procedure==
# Thoroughly clean the intestines using water and salt. Rinse several times until clean.
# Boil the chopped meat and tripe for several minutes until partly cooked.
# Heat a pan and sauté the onions, garlic, ginger, and chilies until fragrant.
# Combine the meat mixture with the sautéed ingredients in a bowl.
# Add black pepper, coriander leaves, and salt.
# Stir in the blood if using.
# Carefully stuff the cleaned intestines with the meat mixture, avoiding overfilling.
# Tie the ends securely with kitchen twine or thin strips of casing.
# Grill the mutura over medium charcoal heat, turning regularly until browned and fully cooked.
# Slice into bite-sized pieces and serve hot.

==Serving==
Mutura is commonly served hot with:
* [[w:Kachumbari|Kachumbari]]
* [[Cookbook:Ugali|Ugali]]
* [[w:Chapati|Chapati]]
* Chili sauce
* Roasted potatoes
* Tea or soft drinks

It is usually eaten as street food, a snack, or a social gathering dish.

==Tips==
* Properly cleaning the intestines improves flavour and hygiene.
* Do not overstuff the casing, as it may burst during grilling.
* Charcoal grilling gives mutura its traditional smoky flavour.
* Turning the sausage regularly helps it cook evenly.
* Fresh coriander and ginger improve aroma and taste.
